result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.which_mutual()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find pairs of mutual (reciprocal) edges in directed graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L23437-L23501){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.which_mutual() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Identifies edge pairs where both A->B and B->A exist, indicating bidirectional connections. Only meaningful for directed graphs. Each pair is returned once with edge IDs in ascending order. This is useful for analyzing reciprocity patterns in social networks, communication graphs, and other directed relationships. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[tuple[int, int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of (edge_id1, edge_id2) tuples representing mutual edge pairs. Empty list if no mutual edges exist. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If called on an undirected graph. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A mutual pair exists whenever both `A -> B` and `B -> A` are present; the edge that has no reciprocal counterpart is excluded from the result: ::: {#f4a20634 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="Alice") .add_node(label="Bob") .add_node(label="Carol") .add_edge("Alice", "Bob") # Edge 1 .add_edge("Bob", "Alice") # Edge 2: mutual with 1 .add_edge("Alice", "Carol") # Edge 3: no reciprocal ) # Returns [(1, 2)]: the only mutual pair graph.which_mutual() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [(1, 2)] ``` ::: ::: The same idea scales to larger communication graphs, where it's useful for isolating which relationships are genuinely bidirectional: ::: {#68002074 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="Alice") .add_node(label="Bob") .add_node(label="Carol") .add_edge(source="Alice", target="Bob") # Edge 1 .add_edge(source="Bob", target="Alice") # Edge 2: mutual with 1 .add_edge(source="Alice", target="Carol") # Edge 3: no reciprocal .add_edge(source="Bob", target="Carol") # Edge 4 .add_edge(source="Carol", target="Bob") # Edge 5: mutual with 4 ) # Returns 2 bidirectional connections len(graph.which_mutual()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 2 ``` ::: :::
